brief.subject: Diesel dips to $6.292, TL carriers push rate hikes
brief.headline: Diesel eases 6 cents as peak inventories back truckload rate push
brief.dek: Diesel slips to $6.292, holiday inventory build supports truckload rate asks, and a lawsuit targets the federal carrier registration system.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 6.0 cents to $6.292 a gallon this week, still up 9.3 cents over four weeks. Meanwhile, a holiday inventory surge is giving truckload carriers leverage in bid season.

sections.heading: Diesel Takes a Small Step Back
bullets: $6.292 per gallon: the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-02.
Down 6.0 cents (0.9%) week over week, a modest break on per-mile fuel costs.
Up 9.3 cents over four weeks, so check that fuel surcharges still match your costs.

sections.heading: Inventory Surge Backs Rate Hikes
bullets: October's Logistics Managers' Index showed a big jump in inventories ahead of the holiday season.
Some truckload carriers are seeking double-digit rate increases, and some have already entered a new bid season.
Stronger peak demand gives small carriers a firmer footing when negotiating rates with shippers and brokers.

sections.heading: Lawsuit Targets Carrier Registration
bullets: The Small Business in Transportation Coalition has filed a legal challenge against a federal carrier registration system.
The system's operators warn that a win could disrupt registration fees for carriers.
State motor carrier safety funding tied to the system could also be affected, so watch for changes in compliance costs.

sections.heading: Demand Signals Look Mixed
bullets: Manufacturing expanded for a 10th straight month, but survey respondents increasingly cited the Iran war and trade wars.
Heavier shipment weights lifted ArcBest's LTL tonnage and revenue per shipment, helping it beat Q3 expectations.
Norfolk Southern and Schneider are partnering to expand East Coast intermodal reach, adding competition for some long-haul lanes.

sections.heading: Walmart Bets Big on Automation
bullets: $6B: Walmart's commitment to automate distribution centers with Symbotic technology.
25 regional facilities will get the systems, aimed at faster inventory replenishment.
Faster DC throughput could change appointment timing and dwell for carriers serving Walmart freight.
